summary: Koné Airport (KNQ/NWWD) is a regional airport serving the west coast town of Koné on Grande Terre, the main island of New Caledonia. It acts as an important gateway to the developing Voh-Koné-Pouembout (VKP) economic zone and the northern half of the territory, providing domestic connections operated primarily by Air Calédonie. The airport supports both business travel linked to the region's nickel mining industry and tourism to the nearby west coast beaches and mountains.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines fly from Koné Airport?
A: Air Calédonie operates scheduled domestic services from Koné, primarily connecting to Nouméa-Magenta and other points on Grande Terre and the Loyalty Islands.

Q: How far is the airport from Koné town centre?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometres east of the town centre, making it a quick drive by car or taxi.

Q: Does Koné Airport have international flights?
A: No, Koné handles domestic flights only. All international traffic is handled by La Tontouta International Airport near Nouméa.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a medium-sized regional airport, it offers basic passenger amenities including a small terminal, car rental desks, and limited food and beverage options.
transport_tips: Rental cars are available at the airport and are recommended for visitors planning to explore the surrounding west coast and the VKP region. Taxis and pre-booked shuttles serve the short route into Koné town, though availability can be limited outside of scheduled flight times. There is no rail or rapid transit connection, so road transport is the only practical option.
local_tip: If visiting the area, take advantage of Koné's location as a base for exploring the stunning west coast scenery, including the nearby Bourail beaches and the inland mountain trails —
